noPlan.decisiveGap: The website route cannot be shown to net $3,000 inside 21 days and $500: beyond unestablished demand, price and close rate, a 50%-deposit / 10-day-build structure settles every balance closed after about day 8 outside the window (SETTLES_IN_TIME), and funding Upwork fixed-price escrow (~$600 per site) for 4 concurrent sites before Stripe's first payout (7-14 days after the first live payment) ties up about $2,400 against the $500 cap (ECONOMICS). Best case nets 4 x ($1,500 - $600 - $60 - $43.80 Stripe fee) - $147 test = $3,037.80, $38 above target, so one sale fewer or one extra cost misses it. The GBP retainer nets $199 per client-month and would need ~16 clients paying inside 21 days.
noPlan.resolution: Run one $147 go/no-go test of the only structure that could fit: payment in full at order and a 5-day build. Day 1: Brain gets 3 Upwork fixed-price quotes for a 5-page site delivered in 5 days. Days 2-7: Brain emails up to 1,500 local businesses without a website via Instantly (deliverability from new domains and finding emails for these businesses are unproven and are measured here). Owner offers a $1,500 site paid 100% upfront. PROOF (day 8): at least 5 full $1,500 payments received AND a quote at or below $600 with 5-day delivery, so designers can be funded from settled payments (about $3,980 net of fees and costs before the test cost) and every site delivered by day 21. STOP (day 8): fewer than 5 full payments, OR no quote at or below $600 for 5-day delivery, OR bounce rate above 5% — then this route cannot carry the goal and Brain researches a different opening that is paid at order and settles within 7 days. There is no undecided band: every outcome on day 8 is proof or stop.

answers.finding: Per-sale net $796.20; 4 sales $3,184.80; less test $3,037.80.
answers.resolution: Accepted: the arithmetic is now in the decisive gap, and the proof gate requires 5 full payments, not 4, so the plan does not ride on a $38 margin.

answers.finding: Timeline: day-9 sale + 10-day build = day 19; balance settles day 21+; first Stripe payout waits 7-14 days.
answers.resolution: Accepted: SETTLES_IN_TIME is now a decisive link; the test only proves the route under 100% upfront payment and a 5-day build, with proof on day 8.

answers.finding: Capital: escrow 4 x $600 = $2,400 vs $500 cap; card exposure $400 understates it.
answers.resolution: Accepted: ECONOMICS is now a decisive link; proof requires designers to be funded from settled customer payments, never from the $500.

answers.finding: Proof/stop quote gates left $701-$900 undecided; new-domain sending and email-finding are unsourced.
answers.resolution: Accepted: single $600 threshold for both proof and stop, plus a bounce-rate stop; deliverability and email-finding are stated as unproven and measured by the test.

answers.finding: GBP retainer rejection arithmetic right ($199 per client-month, ~16 clients).
answers.resolution: Accepted and stated in the decisive gap.

reviews.reasons: Not offering a plan is right (no opening has a single established link beyond reach; Brain's check is NOT_VIABLE), but the revision names the wrong decisive gap for this goal and recommends a test whose success cannot produce the target inside the contract's limits, so the owner would spend $147 learning something that does not decide this goal. Even if the test passes, the website route does not fit 21 days and $500: (1) Timing: proof is on day 9 and each site takes 10 days to build, so a sale closed on the proof day is delivered on day 19 and its balance must be paid and settled by day 21; every sale after day 9 (the 'scale sending' continue path) cannot settle its balance in the window, and only balances count toward net cash kept. Stripe's first payout is 7-14 days after the first live payment (src s6), so deposits taken on days 7-9 may not be usable until day 14-23. (2) Capital: Upwork fixed-price work is funded into escrow when the designer is hired; 4 sites x ~$600 = $2,400 has to be funded around days 7-9, before any Stripe payout, against a $500 cap. With $500 the owner can fund about one site before payouts arrive. (3) Net arithmetic is tight even in the best case: 4 x ($1,500 - $600 - $60 - Stripe ~$43.80) = $3,184.80, minus the $147 test = $3,037.80, $38 above target, so a single extra cost or one sale fewer misses it. The decisiveLinks should include SETTLES_IN_TIME and ECONOMICS (capital tied up), and the resolution should either show how 4 balances settle by day 21 within $500 (e.g. designer paid from settled deposits, faster payment rail, shorter build) or say this route cannot carry the goal and research another.
findings: Timeline: sale day 9 + 10-day build = day 19 delivery; balance payment + ~2 business days settlement = day 21+; first Stripe payout waits 7-14 days after the first live payment.
Capital: escrow 4 x $600 = $2,400 needed before deposits are paid out, vs $500 cap; the card's peakFunding $400 / exposure $400 RECOMMENDATION understates it for more than one concurrent site.

Same test-design issues as d03: proof (quote <= $700) and stop (no quote <= $900) leave $701-$900 undecided; 1,500 emails from new unwarmed domains in days 2-7 and finding emails for businesses with no website are unsourced feasibility assumptions.
GBP retainer rejection is arithmetically right: $299/month minus $100 cost nets $199 per client-month; ~16 clients each paying and settling inside 21 days would be needed.

conditions.why: timeToFirstCash is a RECOMMENDATION (14 days) for the deposit only; the balance that makes the net arrives after a 10-day build, which for any sale after ~day 8 lands outside the 21-day window.
Exposure $400 is a RECOMMENDATION; funding 4 Upwork escrows of ~$600 before Stripe's first payout ties up ~$2,400 against the $500 cap.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is right and the decisive gap is now the one the evidence decides for this goal: beyond unestablished demand, price and close rate, the deposit/10-day-build structure cannot settle balances closed after ~day 8 inside 21 days (SETTLES_IN_TIME) and concurrent Upwork escrow (~$2,400 for 4 sites) cannot be funded within $500 before Stripe's first payout (ECONOMICS); both are in decisiveLinks. The best-case arithmetic is correct and shows how thin the old route was. The resolution is a single go/no-go test of the only structure that could fit (100% upfront, 5-day build), with no undecided band, and a stop that sends Brain to research a different opening paid at order and settling within 7 days. Test spend $147 is inside the $500 cap.
findings: One gap in the proof: designers are 'funded from settled payments', but Stripe's first payout is 7-14 days after the first live payment and only $353 of the cap remains after the test, less than one $600 escrow. If the first payment lands ~day 5 and the payout takes 14 days (day 19), no 5-day build can be funded and delivered by day 21. Add 'first Stripe payout received by ~day 15' (or a faster payment rail) to the proof/stop.
Five $1,500 upfront payments from 1,500 cold emails (0.33%) within days to an unknown vendor is a demanding bar; that is appropriate for a go/no-go, and the plan rightly does not assume it.
Deliverability from new domains and finding emails for businesses with no website are correctly labelled unproven and measured in the test.

noPlan.decisiveGap: The website route cannot be shown to net $3,000 inside 21 days and $500: beyond unestablished demand, price and close rate, a 50%-deposit / 10-day-build structure settles every balance closed after about day 8 outside the window (SETTLES_IN_TIME), and funding Upwork fixed-price escrow (~$600 per site) for 4 concurrent sites before Stripe's first payout (7-14 days after the first live payment) ties up about $2,400 against the $500 cap (ECONOMICS). Best case nets 4 x ($1,500 - $600 - $60 - $43.80 Stripe fee) - $147 test = $3,037.80, $38 above target, so one sale fewer or one extra cost misses it. The GBP retainer nets $199 per client-month and would need ~16 clients paying inside 21 days.
noPlan.resolution: Run one $147 go/no-go test of the only structure that could fit: payment in full at order and a 5-day build. Day 1: Brain gets 3 Upwork fixed-price quotes for a 5-page site delivered in 5 days. Days 2-7: Brain emails up to 1,500 local businesses without a website via Instantly (deliverability from new domains and finding emails for these businesses are unproven and are measured here). Owner offers a $1,500 site paid 100% upfront. PROOF (day 8): at least 5 full $1,500 payments received AND a quote at or below $600 with 5-day delivery, so designers can be funded from settled payments (about $3,980 net of fees and costs before the test cost) and every site delivered by day 21. STOP (day 8): fewer than 5 full payments, OR no quote at or below $600 for 5-day delivery, OR bounce rate above 5% — then this route cannot carry the goal and Brain researches a different opening that is paid at order and settles within 7 days. There is no undecided band: every outcome on day 8 is proof or stop.

answers.finding: Per-sale net $796.20; 4 sales $3,184.80; less test $3,037.80.
answers.resolution: Accepted: the arithmetic is now in the decisive gap, and the proof gate requires 5 full payments, not 4, so the plan does not ride on a $38 margin.

answers.finding: Timeline: day-9 sale + 10-day build = day 19; balance settles day 21+; first Stripe payout waits 7-14 days.
answers.resolution: Accepted: SETTLES_IN_TIME is now a decisive link; the test only proves the route under 100% upfront payment and a 5-day build, with proof on day 8.

answers.finding: Capital: escrow 4 x $600 = $2,400 vs $500 cap; card exposure $400 understates it.
answers.resolution: Accepted: ECONOMICS is now a decisive link; proof requires designers to be funded from settled customer payments, never from the $500.

answers.finding: Proof/stop quote gates left $701-$900 undecided; new-domain sending and email-finding are unsourced.
answers.resolution: Accepted: single $600 threshold for both proof and stop, plus a bounce-rate stop; deliverability and email-finding are stated as unproven and measured by the test.

answers.finding: GBP retainer rejection arithmetic right ($199 per client-month, ~16 clients).
answers.resolution: Accepted and stated in the decisive gap.

review.reasons: NO_PLAN is right and the decisive gap is now the one the evidence decides for this goal: beyond unestablished demand, price and close rate, the deposit/10-day-build structure cannot settle balances closed after ~day 8 inside 21 days (SETTLES_IN_TIME) and concurrent Upwork escrow (~$2,400 for 4 sites) cannot be funded within $500 before Stripe's first payout (ECONOMICS); both are in decisiveLinks. The best-case arithmetic is correct and shows how thin the old route was. The resolution is a single go/no-go test of the only structure that could fit (100% upfront, 5-day build), with no undecided band, and a stop that sends Brain to research a different opening paid at order and settling within 7 days. Test spend $147 is inside the $500 cap.
findings: One gap in the proof: designers are 'funded from settled payments', but Stripe's first payout is 7-14 days after the first live payment and only $353 of the cap remains after the test, less than one $600 escrow. If the first payment lands ~day 5 and the payout takes 14 days (day 19), no 5-day build can be funded and delivered by day 21. Add 'first Stripe payout received by ~day 15' (or a faster payment rail) to the proof/stop.
Five $1,500 upfront payments from 1,500 cold emails (0.33%) within days to an unknown vendor is a demanding bar; that is appropriate for a go/no-go, and the plan rightly does not assume it.
Deliverability from new domains and finding emails for businesses with no website are correctly labelled unproven and measured in the test.

basis.intent: Keep $3,000 of net cash after all direct costs within 21 days, using at most $500 of capital.
